chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abu Khadijah who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Beware that some of you do not refer to the unjust rulers for judgment, but rather look for one of you who knows something of our cases, and make him an arbitrator between you, for I have made him a judge, so refer to him.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْجَوْرِ: The unjust rulers or judges (often referring to the Umayyad/Abbasid caliphs)
key_terms.قَضَايَانَا: Our cases (referring to the legal rulings and traditions of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: How should Shia Muslims handle legal disputes according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam establishes the foundational principle of Shia judicial autonomy during the Minor and Major Ghaibah, directing believers to seek arbitration from those possessing 'ilm al-qada' (knowledge of our affairs) rather than relying on the political authorities of the time. It underscores the continuity of the Imam’s authority through delegated scholars, a concept that later evolved into the theory of Wilayat al-Faqih, ensuring that legal judgments remain aligned with divine law despite the absence of the Infallible Imam.
